contract_plain_english: For N independent random variables with the same distribution, common mean µ, and common finite variance σ², the variance of their sample average is exactly σ²/N.

source_evidence.anchor: Var(X1 + · · · + XN) = Var(X1) + · · · + Var(XN) holds for any independent random variables
source_evidence.location: PDF pages 4-5; printed pages 8-9; Section 1.3 opening
source_evidence.observation: The calculation leading to Equation (1.5) begins under an independence hypothesis.

source_evidence.anchor: If, furthermore, Xi have the same distribution with mean µ and variance σ², then dividing both sides by N²
source_evidence.location: PDF page 5; printed page 9; sentence immediately preceding Equation (1.5)
source_evidence.observation: Equation (1.5) additionally assumes a common distribution, mean µ, and variance σ², and uses quadratic variance scaling under division by N.

source_evidence.anchor: Var((1/N) sum from i=1 to N of Xi) = σ²/N
source_evidence.observation: The equation states the exact variance of the sample mean.

source_evidence.anchor: Var(X) = E(X − E X)²; X : Ω → R
source_evidence.location: PDF page 1; printed page 5; Section 1.1 opening and footnote 1
source_evidence.observation: The variables are real-valued random variables and variance is the expected squared centered value.

binders: Real-valued random variables X₁, ..., X_N on a common probability space.
A common mean µ and common finite variance σ².
definitions_and_conventions: Division of the sum by N scales its variance by 1/N².
hypotheses: X₁, ..., X_N have the same distribution.
Each Xᵢ has mean µ and variance σ².
implicit_context: The independence hypothesis is inherited from the immediately preceding sentence.
The phrase 'If, furthermore' adds identical distribution and common moments without dropping independence.
All variables lie on one probability space.
N is positive, so the normalization by N is defined.
The common variance is finite, as confirmed by the following deduction that σ²/N tends to zero.

details: The left side is the variance of the average, not the average of the variances.
The denominator on the right side is N, resulting from N equal variance terms and the 1/N² scaling.
Identical distribution supplies a single common variance σ² and a common mean µ.
The subsequent limit-to-zero statement is a consequence, not part of the equation itself.

undebatable_constraints: The variables are independent and identically distributed.
The source explicitly mentions both a common mean µ and a common variance σ².
The normalization inside the variance is exactly 1/N.
The right side is exactly σ²/N.
The identity concerns each positive finite sample size N.
Equation (1.5) itself is an equality, not merely an asymptotic limit.
